about: Party groups and caucuses: published evidence of who belongs, one entry per member per list. Made by scripts/groups_from_research.py; see that script for the owner's decisions.

groups.description: Group of left-wing Labour MPs (with some Labour peers) that issues collective statements under the name 'Socialist Campaign Group of Labour MPs'.
groups.description_source: neutral summary; no self-description page found (former website socialistcampaigngroup.com is now a parked domain)

aliases.alias: Socialist Campaign Group of Labour MPs

aliases.note: Very common generic phrase in Hansard ('the WASPI campaign group', 'a local campaign group'). Only count when preceded by 'Socialist' or when 'Labour'/'Labour MPs' is in the same sentence and the speaker is a Labour MP; historically also 'Campaign Group of Labour MPs'.
Initialism also used for unrelated bodies; rare in Hansard. Require the full name earlier in the same speech.

groups.notes: No published membership list found for either Parliament. Lists are signatories of the group's own statements (and contributors to its 2026 pamphlet), so they under-count members (LabourList, 18 Nov 2020, notes some SCG members did not sign) and include peers. Claudia Webbe signed in 2020-21 while sitting as an independent. No signed SCG statement with names was found for 2024-2026 other than the pamphlet. See also the separate entry 'socialist-parliamentary-research-group' (IPSA pooled service) - its relationship to the SCG is not confirmed by any primary source found. Secondary only: Wikipedia infobox and press counts (e.g. New Statesman May 2026 'around 25 members').
groups.name: Socialist Campaign Group

groups.description: A pooled research and writing service registered with IPSA as 'Socialist Parliamentary Research Group (Labour)', funded by subscribing MPs' office budgets.
groups.description_source: IPSA's category label; no self-description found

aliases.note: Initialism; in IPSA data 'FSPRG' is an unrelated web domain charge - exclude.

groups.notes: Included because subscribers overlap heavily with SCG statement signatories, but NO primary source found says SPRG is the SCG's research service. Do not merge with the SCG without confirmation from the group. IPSA claims data for 2025-26 does not yet contain pooled-service claims (checked 2026-11-12).
groups.name: Socialist Parliamentary Research Group
groups.full_name: Socialist Parliamentary Research Group (IPSA pooled staffing service)

groups.description: Caucus of Labour MPs on the party's 'soft left'; chaired in this Parliament by Clive Efford.
groups.description_source: neutral summary; chair as stated by Clive Efford himself in Hansard (2022) and on the Mainstream statement (2025)

aliases.note: Usually means Tribune magazine/newspaper (MPs also claim subscriptions to it). Count only 'Tribune group'/'Tribune Group of MPs'.

groups.notes: No published membership list found for 2019-24 or 2024-. Its January 2026 letter on Andy Burnham's candidacy was sent privately by its executive (New Statesman, Jan 2026); signatories not published. Former website tribunegroup.co.uk returns an empty page. Self-declarations: Clive Efford describes himself as chair (Hansard 2 Feb 2022; Mainstream founding statement Sept 2025). Secondary only: press estimates of 'over 100' MPs.
groups.name: Tribune Group of Labour MPs

groups.description: Group of Labour MPs campaigning for economic growth, planning reform and housebuilding; founded mainly by 2024-intake MPs.
groups.description_source: summary of its July 2024 letter to the Prime Minister and its 2026 report 'An Honest Day' (labourgrowth.co.uk)

aliases.note: Generic; also the Conservative Growth Group (2023-24) and business 'growth groups'. Require 'Labour' or a Labour speaker plus context.
Initialism; rare and ambiguous.

groups.notes: The group's website (labourgrowth.co.uk, accessed 2026-11-12) carries only its 2026 report and names Chris Curtis MP as Parliamentary Chair; no member list. LabourList reported Chris Curtis stepping down as chair in June 2026; the site still names him. Later joint letter (April 2025, with Blue Labour and Red Wall caucuses, on digital ID; c.40 MPs) - full signatory list not found. Secondary only: LabourList/PLMR 'Labour Tribes Mapped' (2025) estimates.
groups.name: Labour Growth Group

groups.description: Blue Labour describes itself as 'a force within the Labour Party committed to the politics of the common good'; a parliamentary caucus of Labour MPs using the name was formed in 2025, convened by Dan Carden.
groups.description_source: bluelabour.org About text (quoted); caucus convenor as described in press

aliases.note: Also names the wider intellectual current (Maurice Glasman, from 2009) - Hansard uses before 2025 refer to that, not the caucus. For 2025-, require 'caucus'/'MPs' or a self-reference.

groups.notes: bluelabour.org (accessed 2026-11-12) lists no parliamentary members. Co-signed the April 2025 digital ID letter with the Labour Growth Group and Red Wall Caucus; full signatory list not found. Secondary only: press names (Carden, Hinder, Brash, Smith etc.).
groups.name: Blue Labour

groups.description: Group of Labour MPs representing 'Red Wall' seats in the North and Midlands, chaired by Jo White MP.
groups.description_source: neutral summary; chair as stated by Jo White to PoliticsHome

aliases.note: 'Red Wall' is a general term for a set of seats; 'Red Wall MPs' is used of Conservatives elected there in 2019. Require 'caucus' or a Labour self-reference after Nov 2024.

groups.notes: No published list found. The caucus runs as a WhatsApp group (PoliticsHome). Co-signed April 2025 digital ID letter (names not fully published). No Hansard hits for 'Red Wall caucus' or 'Red Wall group' on TheyWorkForYou (2026-11-12).
groups.name: Red Wall Caucus

groups.description: 'Mainstream is the home for Labour's radical realists' - a network of Labour members and parliamentarians initiated by Compass and Open Labour (Sept 2025).

aliases.note: Ordinary English word ('mainstream schools'). Count only 'Mainstream' as a proper noun with Labour context, 'Labour Mainstream', or 'Mainstream Labour'.

groups.notes: A party network, not only a caucus of MPs. Publication date taken from TheyWorkForYou Votes' record of the statement (1 Sept 2025); the page itself says 'In September 2025'. Its Interim Council (on /about) includes Alex Sobel MP, Paula Barker MP and Baroness Lister.
groups.name: Mainstream

groups.description: Organisation of the Labour right open to party members (not a caucus of MPs).
groups.notes: No published list of MP members found; website labourfirst.org.uk unreachable from the research environment (proxy 502). Not an MP caucus.
groups.name: Labour First

groups.description: Labour think tank / members' organisation of the party's centre (not a caucus of MPs).
groups.notes: No published list of MP members found. Not an MP caucus.
groups.name: Progressive Britain

groups.description: Joint organising campaign of Labour First and Progress (2020-) within the party.
groups.notes: No published list of MP members found. Not an MP caucus.
groups.name: Labour to Win

groups.description: Think tank and network associated with the party leadership (not a caucus of MPs).

aliases.note: Also an everyday phrase ('Labour together') - require capitalised proper-noun use.

groups.notes: No list of MPs as members; staff/alumni who became MPs are reported by the press only (secondary).
groups.name: Labour Together

groups.description: Labour-affiliated pro-European society; chaired by Stella Creasy MP (self-declared in Hansard). Registered a pooled research service with IPSA.

aliases.note: Initialism; ambiguous.

groups.notes: A party-affiliated society with a wider membership, not only a caucus; included because MPs subscribe to its pooled research service and it is a likely subject of comparison. No published list of MP members found.
groups.name: Labour Movement for Europe

groups.description: Group of Conservative MPs focused on the UK's relationship with the EU; it operates a pooled research service registered with IPSA.
groups.description_source: neutral summary; IPSA describes the ERG as 'a subscription-based pooled service' rather than a membership group

aliases.note: Unambiguous in Brexit-era Commons debate, but 'ERG' is also used for unrelated things (e.g. 'Extremism Risk Guidance', 'Energy Research Group'). Require Conservative/Brexit context or the full name in the same debate.

groups.notes: The ERG has never published a membership list (IPSA FOI RFI-202002-9 and others). The only public record naming MPs is IPSA's expense data for subscriptions to its pooled research service, which IPSA says is not a membership list. 2017-19 Parliament claims (12 MPs, financial year 2019-20 before the Dec 2019 election) are in ipsa_pooled.json but not listed here. Secondary only: press tallies (e.g. PoliticsHome Mar 2025).
groups.name: European Research Group

groups.description: Caucus of Conservative MPs who identify with 'one nation' conservatism (formed March 2019).

aliases.note: Usually the caucus in 2019-24 Conservative speech, but 'one nation' is a general political phrase used by all parties (and 'One Nation Labour'). Require 'Conservative'/'caucus'/'group of Conservative MPs'.
Highly ambiguous: Disraeli tradition, 'One Nation Labour' (2012-15), Pauline Hanson's One Nation (Australia). Do not use alone.

groups.notes: No full membership list was ever published by the group (secondary sources agree). Its website onenationconservatives.co.uk is now a gambling spam site; the Wayback availability API returned only a 2025 snapshot (spam era), so earlier snapshots could not be checked from this environment. Possible category-3 evidence: individual MPs announced membership on Twitter/X in 2019-20 (cited by Wikipedia) - not verified here. A 2019 Observer op-ed 'One Nation conservatism can make a success of Brexit' (18 May 2019) was signed by five leading members - 2017-19 Parliament, out of scope.
groups.name: One Nation Conservatives

groups.description: Group of Conservative MPs and peers chaired by Sir John Hayes; its 2021 collection is subtitled 'Conservative Thinking for a Post-Liberal Age'. Registered a pooled research service with IPSA.
groups.description_source: title of the group's 2021 publication; neutral summary

aliases.note: 'common sense' is an everyday phrase; capitalised 'Common Sense Group' is fairly specific, but transcripts may lower-case it. Require 'Group' and Conservative context.

aliases.alias: Common Sense Group of Conservative MPs

groups.notes: No group-published membership list found. Its 9 Nov 2020 letter to The Daily Telegraph (paywalled) is reproduced in full, with all 28 signatories, on Sir Edward Leigh MP's own website - used here. The letter says the group then had '59 Conservative MPs and seven peers'. The 2021 essay collection 'Common Sense: Conservative Thinking for a Post-Liberal Age' names contributors; a copy was not located. IPSA subscriber data (2021-24) is also listed. No post-2024 list found.
groups.name: Common Sense Group

groups.description: Group of Conservative MPs from the North of England (chaired by Jake Berry in 2020-24). Registered a pooled research service with IPSA.

aliases.note: Initialism; ambiguous.

groups.notes: No group-published membership list found (website northernresearchgroup.co.uk unreachable; Wayback blocked from this environment). Letters (Oct 2020, Jan 2021) were reported without full names. IPSA subscribers 2021-24 only. Group appears inactive after the 2024 election (refunds in Dec 2024).
groups.name: Northern Research Group

groups.description: Group of Conservative MPs founded in 2020 to examine UK policy on China (founders include Tom Tugendhat and Neil O'Brien).

aliases.note: Also used for the Covid Recovery Group. Do not use alone.

groups.notes: No published membership list found; chinaresearchgroup.org now redirects to an unrelated site. Not a registered IPSA pooled service.
groups.name: China Research Group

groups.description: 'Our caucus is comprised of MPs, MSPs, and peers who are united around conservative environmentalist principles and champion greater environmental action in Parliament.'

aliases.note: Initialism; ambiguous (e.g. European standards body CEN).

groups.notes: The only Conservative group found with a current, group-published membership list. Ministers and whips are not eligible to join (press). The current page is undated - record the access date and re-check. CEN Fellows are former MPs and MSPs are not UK parliamentarians; both are included as published but flagged. Party shown is the Members API 'latest party' - check defections.
groups.name: Conservative Environment Network

groups.description: Group of mainly 2019-intake Conservative MPs co-chaired by Miriam Cates and Danny Kruger (May 2023 - July 2024); published a migration plan in July 2023.

aliases.note: Also a generic phrase ('the new Conservatives', 'new Conservative MPs'). Require capitalised group use in 2023-24.

groups.notes: Group website thenewconservatives.co.uk now returns 404; Wayback could not be reached from this environment, so any member/supporter list it carried is unverified. Press reproduced supporter lists (secondary). Defunct since July 2024.
groups.name: New Conservatives

groups.description: Group of Conservative MPs (2020-22) chaired by Mark Harper with Steve Baker as deputy, opposing Covid restrictions.

aliases.note: Also used of government/devolved 'Covid recovery groups' (e.g. Anas Sarwar, Scottish Parliament). Require Conservative/Westminster context.
Also the China Research Group.

groups.notes: Letters (Nov 2020 c.70 MPs; Feb 2021 c.63 MPs) were reported with signatory counts but names were not published. Steve Baker repeatedly referred to 'declarations ... in connection to the Covid Recovery Group' (Register of Members' Financial Interests) - a possible category-3 source not checked here.
groups.name: Covid Recovery Group

groups.description: Group of Conservative MPs and peers (2021-24) chaired by Craig Mackinlay, scrutinising the cost of net zero policies.
groups.description_source: neutral summary; chair self-declared in Hansard

aliases.note: Initialism.

groups.notes: The group never published a membership list. Its 2 Jan 2022 Sunday Telegraph letter is paywalled; no verbatim reproduction by a signatory was found. Andrew Lewer publicly explained why he signed (Northampton Chronicle, Jan 2022 - page blocked here). The 12 Feb 2022 fracking letter (29 MPs + 1 peer) and a Mar 2022 Daily Mail letter had unpublished names. DeSmog's profile page lists 'members' attributed to the Feb 2022 letter, whose names it elsewhere says were not published - not used.
groups.name: Net Zero Scrutiny Group

groups.description: Group of Conservative MPs promoting 'blue collar conservatism', convened by Esther McVey (2019-24).

aliases.note: Generic adjective.

groups.notes: Former website bluecollarconservatism.co.uk is now a gambling spam site; any member list it once carried could not be checked (Wayback unreachable from this environment).
groups.name: Blue Collar Conservatives

groups.description: Group of Conservative MPs (2022-24) chaired by Ranil Jayawardena advocating tax cuts and supply-side reform.

aliases.note: Also the Labour Growth Group.

groups.notes: No published list found.
groups.name: Conservative Growth Group

groups.description: Movement launched February 2024 (Liz Truss, Mark Littlewood) within the Conservative Party.
groups.notes: Not a caucus with members; launch attendance was reported by press only.
groups.name: Popular Conservatives

groups.description: Pooled staffing service so named in IPSA data (2021-22 only); no self-description found.
groups.notes: Four Conservative MPs claimed for it in 2021-22 (Andrew Bowie, Gareth Bacon, James Davies, Robin Millar) per IPSA data. Purpose not established; listed for completeness only.
groups.name: Conservative Union Research Group
groups.full_name: Conservative Union Research Group (IPSA pooled service)

groups.description: Internal Liberal Democrat group promoting 'four-cornered liberalism'; open to party members.
groups.notes: Party members' organisation, not a caucus of MPs. No list of MP members found (liberalreform.org.uk home page accessed; socialliberal.net returned 403).
groups.name: Liberal Reform

groups.description: Internal Liberal Democrat pressure group promoting social liberalism; open membership.
groups.notes: Party members' organisation, not a caucus of MPs. No list of MP members found (liberalreform.org.uk home page accessed; socialliberal.net returned 403).
